Leader Rooted in Humanity

"I have always been drawn to things that hadn't been done before — and to the people it takes to do them."

Squadron Leader Sarnish Kour (Retired) has spent nearly two decades building things that did not exist before: missions, teams, institutions, and ideas. A military officer in the Indian Air Force, an operations leader at Willis Towers Watson, and a leader of strategy and operations at Thapar Institute of Engineering & Technology, she brings the same quiet discipline to every room she enters, and carries the same lesson into every setting: people first, mission always.

She is currently a doctoral researcher at LM Thapar School of Management, studying how entrepreneurs develop opportunities for social impact — a question she has been living, not just researching, for years.

What I Believe
☸
Sarbat Da Bhala — for everyone's good
A Punjabi phrase meaning the wellbeing of all. It is a prayer and a principle — the belief that no decision made in isolation is truly sound, and that the measure of any action is what it does for the world beyond yourself. I carry this in every role I have held: in the Air Force, in institution-building, in research on social ventures that exist precisely to serve those the market overlooks.
☸
Integrity is the baseline
Everything else — strategy, influence, relationships — is built on top of this. Without it, nothing else holds. It is not a value I aspire to. It is the one I refuse to negotiate. In uniform, in boardrooms, in research — the standard has stayed the same.
☸
Reverence for all that exists
Not just people. Every stone, every creature, every quiet thing that sustains life deserves respect. A stone that supports a fish in the water, the soil that holds a tree — nothing on this earth is without consequence. This is not sentiment. It is a way of paying attention, and of recognising that we share this earth, not own it.
☸
Know what is yours to carry
Most of what we worry about is not in our control. Most of what we can change, we leave untouched. Clarity about this distinction — what is mine to act on, what is not — is where effective leadership and a calmer life both begin. Ten years in the Air Force reinforced this: when the stakes are real, it is the difference between decisive action and paralysis.
☸
Choose your battles
Not every hill is worth holding. The leaders who endure know which fights matter, when to push, and when to let go — and who can tell the difference in the moment, not only in hindsight. I have been in rooms where everything felt urgent. The ones who moved things forward were rarely the loudest. They were the most discerning.
A Decade in Blue

Indian Air Force

Ten years as a commissioned officer in the Indian Air Force: the foundation of everything that came after.

2008
Answering a childhood calling
Indian Air Force

The uniform had been a dream since childhood, along with a deep urge to serve the nation. Though she had begun a promising career in information technology, selected by both Infosys and TCS, Sarnish answered that calling and joined the Indian Air Force. Officer training at the Air Force Academy was followed by a year at the Air Force Technical College, where she earned a PG Diploma in Aeronautical Engineering.

2008 –
2013
Missiles, by choice
Indian Air Force

Inspired by Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam, she chose to specialise in Surface-to-Air missile systems. She stood first in the missile technical training course, and later first in order of merit in the professional knowledge course among more than 50 officers. These years brought operations and deployments, including live missile firing at the test range built by Dr. Kalam, where she was part of the team that validated refurbished systems alongside Russian specialists. Alongside her technical role, she held the additional appointment of squadron adjutant, overseeing administration and welfare for around 500 personnel.

The journey back from that firing, several days by military train alongside some 120 air warriors, remains one of her most formative memories of service.

2013 –
2015
Squadron Leader
Indian Air Force

Promoted to Squadron Leader, she led her teams through regular deployments, and her squadron hosted a combined Air Defence exercise with the Army at Pokhran.

2015 –
2018
Building, not buying
Indian Air Force

As a Production Engineer at a Base Repair Depot, she led sections of around 250 personnel working across missile, radar and communication systems. She led the indigenous fabrication of critical defence equipment with an Indian vendor at ₹8 crore, saving the exchequer ₹32 crore against import. The work earned a Commendation from the Air Officer Commanding-in-Chief, Maintenance Command, and was showcased by the IAF Innovation Display Team during the Air Force Day celebrations in October 2017, where she presented it to the then President of India, Shri Ram Nath Kovind, and the then Union Defence Minister, Smt. Nirmala Sitharaman.

In the depot’s Explosive Ordnance Disposal lab, her team revamped the transmitters and receivers of the HOBO robotic vehicles, and she trained the operating units on the upgraded systems.

2017 –
2018
Preparing for the next chapter
Indian Air Force

Selected for the residential Pre-Release Course at IIM Indore, she went on to join Willis Towers Watson after completing her service.

What the uniform taught

The Short Service Commission is a ten-year chapter by design. Sarnish served it in full, and carried forward the principle it built: people first, mission always. The mission always matters, but it is people who achieve it. Look after them, and they will carry the mission further than any order could.

She learned to lead where the margin for error was zero, and the only currency that mattered was trust.

Corporate Experience

Willis Towers Watson

From the discipline of service to the language of business: building an offshore operation from the ground up for US and UK clients.

2018
A new kind of mission
Willis Towers Watson

Sarnish joined Willis Towers Watson through the IIM Indore placement process. In her interview, the conversation turned naturally to her years in the Air Force: combat vehicles, deployments, missile firings, and the air warriors she led. When the panel smiled that the firm had no combat vehicles, only computers and laptops, she saw no contradiction. The essentials travel well: a sense of urgency, an awareness that every action has consequences, and the commitment, discipline and care that leadership demands. In business, the client’s need becomes the mission, and your team are still your people.

She joined the Mumbai centre as Operations Manager for actuarial pension valuations, serving US and UK clients, including Fortune 500 companies. The work carried a quiet weight: retirement valuations help secure the pensions people depend on after a lifetime of work. For her, it was a mission close to the heart, serving people’s security and dignity in later life.

Jul –
Nov 2018
Listening to the business
Willis Towers Watson

She led the first consolidated Voice of Business Partner survey for Great Britain, covering around 3,000 performers, giving stakeholders a single, structured view of how the teams were serving them.

Nov 2018 –
Mar 2019
Planning for the unexpected
Willis Towers Watson

She designed the business continuity plan for the UK & Ireland pension administration team: around 120 people across Mumbai, Manila and the UK, with clear priorities and transfer protocols in case any site was disrupted.

2018 –
2021
Building from the ground up
Willis Towers Watson

She stabilised a newly established offshore valuation operation, at a time when the actuarial team itself was being set up, and continuously strengthened its effectiveness through operating frameworks, workflow and time tracking, quality-control checks, and performance systems. Within the first year, the client portfolio grew threefold, with consistently high Voice of Business Partner scores from US and UK stakeholders.

2018 –
2021
Investing in people
Willis Towers Watson

She rebuilt the team from 10 to more than 85 people and brought attrition down from 28% to near zero through structured performance measurement, a Route to Competency model, and succession planning. She also served on the Internal Complaints Committee.

What the corporate world taught

The essentials had indeed travelled. Systems create stability, but people create performance, and when you look after your people, they deliver for the client every time.

Academia

Thapar Institute of
Engineering & Technology

Many paths, one purpose: helping one of India’s oldest and finest institutions extend its reach, earn global recognition, and prepare its students for the future.

2022
Joining for accreditation
LM Thapar School of Management

Sarnish joined LM Thapar School of Management, the AACSB-accredited management school of Thapar Institute, as Manager – Accreditation & Rankings. The role grew naturally as she took on admissions, marketing, outreach, and the full experience of the school’s international students.

2022 –
2025
Guiding students on their path
LM Thapar School of Management

For Sarnish, admissions were always about helping students find the right path to their careers. She delivered 232 admissions against a target of 200, closing the intake early. She guided 21 international and national students in the MaRIHE programme through every part of their journey, from arrival to academic support. She represented the school at MaRIHE Consortium meetings in Finland and Porto, and took students to Japan for internships, sustainability coursework and cultural immersion.

2023 –
2025
Reaching further
Thapar Institute of Engineering & Technology

As Manager – Marketing & Admissions for the institute, she built its digital outreach and enrolment operations at scale: CRM systems across the full admissions lifecycle, pan-India tele-calling, and regional outreach offices in Dehradun and Amritsar, alongside a range of institutional projects.

2024
In the classroom
Thapar School of Liberal Arts & Sciences

She taught Organisational Change & Development, an HRM specialisation course, to sixth-semester students at the Thapar School of Liberal Arts & Sciences.

2024 –
2026
A world first
Thapar Institute of Engineering & Technology

The EFMD Business School Impact System (BSIS) had only ever been awarded to business schools. Thapar set out to be assessed as a whole university, engineering and management together. Working alongside a core team of professors from across departments, Sarnish coordinated the effort end to end. She structured the plan, set the deadlines, and served as the point of contact with the BSIS experts, from the first documents to the review visit in February 2026, while also contributing directly to the work on the impact dimensions. In 2026, Thapar became the first full university in the world to receive the BSIS Impact Label.

2025 –
Present
Head – Brand Strategy, Communications & Operations
Thapar Institute of Engineering & Technology

Official designation: Head – Marketing & Admissions

Today she leads strategy and operations across enrolment, brand, communications, outreach and accreditation, reporting to the Vice Chancellor. She also represents the institute at national industry forums such as FICCI, and at international consortia and conferences.

What these years taught

Seeking excellence is never a solo pursuit. The milestones that matter most are reached together, through shared purpose, patient effort, and trust built along the way.

Education

Relearn.

School
Where it all began
Cosmic Heart Senior Secondary School, Kathua · J&K State Board

Sarnish finished her Matriculation first in her school, first in her district, and fifth in the state, earning a full scholarship for her higher secondary years, where she studied both the medical and non-medical science streams side by side. Her early curiosity took her to the National Children’s Science Congress, where she presented a project on saving electricity at Bengal Engineering College, Shibpur, and to the CSIR Programme on Youth for Leadership in Science. Along the way came prizes in debates, symposia and science quizzes.

Above all, these were years shaped by the guidance of the school’s principal, Swami Paramanand, whose ideals continue to shape her outlook on life.

What learning taught

Learning, for her, has one purpose: to create impact. If not in the lives of many, then at least in the lives of a few.

🎓 Research

Doctoral Work &
Publications

Sarnish's doctoral research at LM Thapar School of Management (AACSB-accredited) studies how social entrepreneurs develop opportunities for impact, and the role perspective-taking (understanding the thoughts, feelings and motivations of others) plays in that process. Her work proposes a process view of how impact opportunities take shape in social ventures.

Life Beyond Work

01

What she writes

Poems written when something needed to be said differently.

🌸
'Low' or 'Hollow'
Reflection · 2022
"Have you ever felt low?
Why would you not have?"
Have you ever felt low?
Why would you not have? We are all feeling beings With clowns and frowns With Ups and downs!!
Maybe when your plans are not going straight, Or when you don't get something even after a long wait. Maybe when you have been ditched by dear mates, Or by lovely memories or scenes that tune re-creates. For you, when nobody stands the expected ground, And when you are all alone with no one around. It's perfectly okay if at times you feel low, You are still fortunate to be able to let that feeling go.
However,
Do you know how it is to feel hollow?
When it's unbearable that you have lost somebody so dear, Or the question – 'Why me' is not answered clear.
When you feel lonely in a gathering, When your tears wonder – is someone even bothering.
Earned in years and you have lost those crowns, When you can feel all the time – the never healing wounds.
When you so much want to walk that past again, This time through different choices and different lanes.
Having lost yourself for someone who doesn't even realise, Scary are the moments – when you hear that hollow shrieking noise.
But please do remember – You have come so far and there's nothing you cannot cope, Go to a friend or a listening stranger or a professional help, but don't forget ever – You and the God within you are unbeatable hope.
— Sarnish
🌷
Can Love Be A 'Maybe'?
Reflection · Love
"I loved you. I love you.
I will love you, maybe."
I loved you. I love you.I will love you, maybe.
I tried. I cried.I adjusted. I compromised.I sacrificed. I tolerated.I controlled. I changed.
I needed you. I valued you.I cared for you. I treasured you.I trusted you. I gathered you.I cherished you. I celebrated you.I supported you. I loved you.
You ditched me. You demeaned me.You left me. You isolated me.You disgraced me. You compared me.You changed me. You mistreated me.You hurt me. You loved me?You lost me.
I am desolated. I am alone.I am depressed. I am dejected.I am unhappy. I am worthless.I am guilty. I am bad.I am done.
I quit, but I loved you. I love you. I will love you, may be.
— Sarnish
